That on receipt of call at 100 number, DD No. 52A dated 07.11.2012 was lodged, upon which present case was registered and investigation was carried out.
CHARGE 3.
Vide order dated 09.02.2015, notice under Section 251 Cr.P.C. was served upon the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 279/337/338/304A to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the matter was fixed for prosecution evidence and in order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined 15 witnesses.
EVIDENCE 4. PW-1 is Praveen, who deposed that on the day of incident, he, Manoj, Harpal and Sittu were coming from the SRHC Hospital side in a Maruti Van.
Upon reaching the Mansa Devi Road, near CNG Pump, Narela, the offending vehicle came at a high speed from the front side in a rash and negligent manner and hit against their Maruti Van.
Due to the collision, their Maruit Van was severally damaged and they all sustained injuries.
They were taken to SRHC Hospital where Manoj succumbed to his injuries.
He has proved the site plan as Ex.PW1/A, arrest memo of accused as Ex.PW1/B and his personal search memo as Ex.PW1/C.
He has also identified the offending vehicle and Maruti Van through photographs Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
PW-2 Harpal and PW3 Sittu also deposed on the similar lines.
They deposed that the offending vehicle came from the left side and was trying to cross the road at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner.
They however, could not identify the accused, having become unconscious after the accident but identified both the vehicles involved in the accident through photographs Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
PW-4 Shri Chand is the father of deceased Manoj, who had identified the dead body of his son vide identification memo Ex.PW4/A and proved the dead body handing over memo as Ex.PW4/B.
PW-5 is Krishan is the registered owner of the offending vehicle who pursuant to the notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicle Act produced the accused as the driver of the vehicle in question.
He identified the notice under Section 133 M.V. Act; proved the reply as Ex.PW5/A and superdignama of the said tractor as Ex.PW5/B.
PW-6 SI Amit deposed that on the date of incident, on receipt of DD No.52A, he along with IO HC Ram Niwas went to the site and found the two vehicles in question in accidental condition.
The injured persons had already been removed to SRHC Hospital.
Upon receipt of rukka, handed over by the IO, he went to the PS, got registered the FIR, came back at the spot and handed over the copy of FIR and original rukka to the second IO SI Satbir.

PW-7 Dr. Bhim Singh conducted the postmortem of deceased Manoj on 08.11.2012 at BJRM Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi, vide report Ex.PW7/A and opined the injuries to the ante mortem in Surender vs The State on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11458284/
2 nature and consistent with a road vehicular accident.
PW-8 ASI Kusumpal, duty officer proved the copy of the FIR as Ex.PW8/A and endorsement on the rukka Ex.PW8/B.

PW-9 ASI Suresh Kumar, DD writer proved the copy of DD entry as Ex.PW9/A.
PW-10 Ct. Satbir had accompanied the IO SI Satbir to the spot where they found the Maruti Van in accidental condition.

With the help of the crame the said van was removed to Central Malkhaha,
Narela.

He deposed that he along with the IO went to SRHC Hospital and collected the dead body of deceased Manoj and took the dead body to BJRM Hospital for postmortem and after postmortem,
dead body was handed over the relatives of the deceased.
PW-11 ASI Ram Niwas is the first investigating officer who has deposed on the lines of PW6 SI Amit.
He also deposed that after leaving ASI Amit at the spot, he left for SRHC Hospital to see the injured but they were not in a condition to give any statement that day.

He collected MLC of the injured persons and returned to the spot; took photographs of the spot Ex.P1 to Ex.P10, prepared the rukka and made endorsement thereon vide Ex.PW11/A, seized both the vehicles vide memos Ex.PW11/B and Ex.PW11/C and sent the offending vehicle with the help of a crane to Central Malkhana.
Necessary documents were eventually handed over to the second IO SI Satbir.
PW-12 (Retd.) SI Satbir is the second Investigating Officer of the present case.
He deposed on the lines of PW-10 Ct. Satbir.
He took the custody of the accidental van from the spot and of the trolley tractor already stationed at Malkhana and seized the same.
He deposed that he sent the dead body of deceased Manoj at BJRM mortuary after identification vide memo Ex.PW4/A and Ex.PW12/A.

He recorded the statement of injured as SRHC Hospital, served a notice U/s 133 MV Act to the owner of the offending tractor vide Ex.PW5/A to which the owner replied vide Ex.12/B and produced the accused at the PS on 11.11.2012 pursuant to which the latter was arrested and his DL was seized, witness also seized the insurance and RC of the offending vehicle vide Ex.PW12/C and Ex.PW12/D.
Thereafter, he sent both the vehicles for the mechanical inspection vide Ex.12/E and Ex.PW12/F.
He also collected the postmortem report of deceased and after completion of investigation, filed the charge-sheet in the court.
He also identified the vehicles through photographs Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
He prepared the site plan on 11.11.2012 at the instance of PW Praveen.

PW-13 Dr. Rajesh Kumar, SMO, SRHC Hospital has proved the MLCs of the injured Harpal,
Praveen and Manoj as Ex.PW13/A, Ex.PW13/B and Ex.PW13/C wherein injuries sustained by injured Harpal were opined to be simple; injures sustained by injured Praveen were opined to be grievous while injured Manoj was declared brought dead.

PW-14 ASI Rajesh has proved entry at serial no.646 in Register No.19 vide which the case property was deposited in the Malkhana as Ex.PW14/A. PW-15 ASI Rajender Singh was on PCR duty on the date of incident and took one of the injured to SRHC Hospital.

5. During the course of evidence, statement of accused was recorded on 19.02.2019 under Section 294 Cr.P.C. where he did not dispute the identity of certain documents and admitted the mechanical inspection report dated 11.11.2012 of the two vehicles already Ex.PW12/E and Ex.PW12/F.

3 5.
After closure of prosecution evidence, statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C was recorded on 21.02.2019 in which appellant pleads innocence and false implication.
No DE was led by the appellant.
6. I have heard ld. Counsel for the appellant/convict and Ld. Addl. PP for the State and perused the record carefully.
GROUNDS OF APPEAL 7.

Aggrieved by the judgment of conviction 11.09.2019 and order on sentence dated 23.09.2019 passed by Ld. MM, North, Rohini Courts, the present appeal has been preferred on the ground that the said judgment has been passed in mechanical manner.

It is stated that the findings of the Ld.
Trial Court are contrary to the record and the facts / evidence placed on the record does not warrant conviction, as there are number of contradictions in the testimonies of the material witnesses.
Therefore, it is prayed that the judgment of conviction and order on sentence are liable to be set aside and appellant is liable to be acquitted.

8. On the other hand, Ld. Addl. PP for the State has strongly controverted the above arguments of the Ld. Counsel for the appellant/convict and has argued that there is no illegality or infirmity in the judgment under challenge, which has been passed after considering all the evidence on the record.
9. Heard.
Trial Court Record perused.
FINDINGS 10.
The ld. Trial court vide judgment dated 11.09.2019 observed that case of the prosecution has been proved.

11. It was incumbent upon the prosecution to prove the following ingredients to establish the guilt of the accused under Section 279 and 304A IPC:
(i) The accused was driving his vehicle on a public way and caused the accident.
(ii) It must have been caused by rash or negligent act/driving of the accused.
(iii) The death so caused, must be causa causans of the rash and negligent act/driving of the accused.

12. To impose criminal liability under this Section, it is necessary that the death should have been the direct result of a rash and negligent act of the accused and that act must be proximate cause without the intervention of another's negligence.
It must be the causa causans: it is not enough that it may have been the causa sine qua non.

Surender vs The State on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11458284/
4 13.
Rash or negligent act is an act done and intentionally or designedly.

A rash act is primarily an over hasty act and is thus opposed to a deliberate act but it also includes an act which, though it may be said to be deliberate is yet done without due deliberation and caution.

Negligence is the breach of a duty caused by omission to do something which a reasonable man guided by those considerations which ordinarily regulate the conduct of human affairs, would do, or the doing of something which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
Negligence is the genus of which rashness is a specie.

In order that rashness or negligence may be criminal, it must be of such a degree as to amount to taking hazard knowing that the hazard was of such a degree that injury was most likely to be caused thereby.
The criminality lies in running the risk or doing such an act, with recklessness and indifference to the consequences.

Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Baba Chandra Vs. State of Maharashtra 1968 SC 1319 held that:
"Criminal negligence is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen, it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted.''
9.

entities.text: Baba Chandra Vs. State of Maharashtra 1968 SC 1319
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Culpable rashness is acting with consciousness that the mischievous and illegal consequences may follow, but with the hope that FIR No.648/95 5/10 they will not,
and often with the belief that the actor has taken sufficient precaution to prevent their happening.

The imputability arises from acting despite the consciousness."
14.
I have carefully perused the testimony of PW1, PW2 and PW3, who were the star prosecution witnesses.

Vide their testimonies, they have proved the presence of accused and the factum of accident taking place on 07.11.2012, wherein Harpal, sustained simple injuries and Praveen sustained grievous injuries and the deceased Manoj was fatally injured.
The factum of accident has not been disputed by the accused even in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
Even the identity of the offending vehicle has not been disputed by the accused.

The death of the deceased Manoj having been caused as a result of road accident, also stands proved by the postmortem report proved as Ex.PW7/A, wherein it had been opined that the death was due to coma and shock consequent upon multiple injuries and all the injuries were ante mortem, fresh and could be caused by blunt force/surface impact.
The testimony of PW1 was duly corroborated with the testimony of PW2 and PW3.
The testimony of PW1, who was with the deceased at the time of incident does not suffer from any infirmity and is found to be trustworthy and natural.
15. Thus, after perusal of the record and the findings given, there is no illegality in the judgment dated 11.09.2019 and the ld.
Trial court has thus rightly convicted the accused for the offence punishable under Section 279/337/338/304A IPC and the judgment dated 11.09.2019 is upheld.

COMING TO THE POINT OF SENTENCE 16.
The Court is mindful of the sentencing policy and its impact on all the stakeholders.
"......The law regulates social interests, arbitrates conflicting claims an demands.
Security of persons and property of the people is an essential function of the State.
It could be achieved through instrumentality of criminal law.
Undoubtedly, there is a cross cultural conflict where living law must find answer to the new challenges and the courts are required to mould the sentencing system to meet the challenges.
The contagion of lawlessness would undermine social order and lay it in ruins.
Protection of society and stamping out criminal proclivity must be the object of law which must be achieved by imposing appropriate sentence.

Therefore, law as a corner-stone of the edifice of "order"
should meet the challenges confronting the society.

Friedman in his "Law in Changing Society"
stated that, "State of criminal law continues to be - as it should be - a decisive reflection of social consciousness of society".
Therefore, in operating the sentencing system, law should adopt the corrective machinery or the deterrence based on factual matrix.
By deft modulation sentencing process be stern where it should be, and tempered with mercy where it warrants to be.

The facts and given circumstances in each case, the nature of the crime, the manner in which it was planned and committed, the motive for commission of the crime, the conduct of the accused, the nature of weapons used and all other attending circumstances are relevant facts which would enter into the area of consideration.

Therefore, undue sympathy to impose inadequate sentence would do more harm to the justice system to undermine the public confidence in the efficacy of law and society could not long endure under such serious threats.
It is, therefore, the duty of every court to award proper sentence having regard to the nature of the offence and the manner in which it was executed or committed etc.
This position was illuminatingly stated by this Court in Sevaka Perumal etc. v. State of Tamil Nadu (1991 (3) SCC 471).

entities.text: Sevaka Perumal etc. v. State of Tamil Nadu (1991 (3) SCC 471)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The criminal law adheres in general to the principle of proportionality in prescribing liability according to the culpability of each kind of criminal conduct.

It ordinarily allows some significant discretion to the Judge in arriving at a sentence in each case, presumably to permit sentences that reflect more subtle considerations of culpability that are raised by the special facts of each case.
Judges in essence affirm that punishment ought always to fit the crime; yet in practice sentences are determined largely by other considerations.
Sometimes it is the correctional needs of the perpetrator that are offered to justify a sentence.

Sometimes the desirability of keeping him out of circulation,
and sometimes even the tragic results of his crime.
Inevitably these considerations cause a departure from just desert as the basis of punishment and create cases of apparent injustice that are serious and widespread.
Proportion between crime and punishment is a goal respected in principle, and in spite of errant notions, it remains a strong influence in the determination of sentences.

The practice of punishing Surender vs The State on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11458284/
6 all serious crimes with equal severity is now unknown in civilized societies, but such a radical departure from the principle of proportionality has disappeared from the law only in recent times.
Even now for a single grave infraction drastic sentences are imposed.
Anything less than a penalty of greatest severity for any serious crime is thought then to be a measure of toleration that is unwarranted and unwise.

But in fact, quite apart from those considerations that make punishment unjustifiable when it is out of proportion to the crime, uniformly disproportionate punishment has some very undesirable practical consequences."
17. Reliance is placed upon Shailesh Jasvantbhai & Anr vs State Of Gujarat & Ors Appeal (Crl.) 118 of 2006 DOD by Supreme Court, 19 January, 2006.

entities.text: Shailesh Jasvantbhai & Anr vs State Of Gujarat & Ors Appeal (Crl.) 118 of 2006

sentences.text: Normally the Appellate Court would not interfere in the discretion exercised by the Ld. Trial Court in awarding the sentence or fine.

However, in the interest of justice, since the matter pertains to the year 2012 and convict, who is a senior citizen, has already undergone trial for a considerable time of almost 11 years, there is no other previous involvement of the convict which has been brought to the knowledge of the court and accordingly as per Section 386(b) (iii) Cr.P.C. without altering the finding given by the ld.
Trial court
Order on sentence passed by ld. Trial Court dated 23.09.2019 is modified to this extent.

7 20.
In view of the above discussion, the appeal is disposed off accordingly.

Appellant is directed to appear before Ld. Trial Court on 29.04.2023.
21.

22. Appeal file be consigned to record room.
